claims.text: When summarizing scientific texts, large language models omit details that limit the scope of research conclusions.
Even when explicitly prompted for accuracy, most large language models produce broader generalizations of scientific results than those present in the original texts.
DeepSeek, ChatGPT-4o, and LLaMA 3.3 70B overgeneralize scientific results in 26% to 73% of cases.
Large language model-generated science summaries are nearly five times more likely to contain broad generalizations compared to human-authored summaries.
Newer large language models tend to perform worse in generalization accuracy than earlier models when summarizing scientific research.

evidence.description: Evaluation of 4900 LLM-generated summaries showed DeepSeek, ChatGPT-4o, and LLaMA 3.3 70B overgeneralizing in 26–73% of cases.
Direct comparison between LLM-generated and human-authored science summaries yielded an odds ratio of 4.85 (95% CI [3.06, 7.70], p < 0.001) for broad generalizations.
Testing across 10 prominent LLMs demonstrated that newer models tended to perform worse in generalization accuracy than earlier ones.

methodologies.name: LLM Scientific Summarization Evaluation
methodologies.description: Evaluation comparing 4,900 LLM-generated summaries from 10 prominent LLMs against original scientific texts and human-authored summaries for generalization bias.
conditions: tested across 10 LLMs including ChatGPT-4o, ChatGPT-4.5, DeepSeek, LLaMA 3.3 70B, and Claude 3.7 Sonnet

future_work.text: Lowering LLM temperature settings as a potential mitigation strategy for generalization bias.
